1011.event_title: General Ludwig Beck resigns rather than prepare an attack on Czechoslovakia
1011.event: As chief of the German army general staff, Ludwig Beck sent Hitler memoranda in 1938 opposing the planned attack on Czechoslovakia. In the summer of 1938 he urged the senior generals to resign together to prevent a European war; when they would not, he stepped down from his post alone that August.
1011.explanation: Beck recoiled from a deed he judged wrong even though going along with it was the safe and expected course, and he became a leading figure of the German resistance.
1011.tie_back: Valluvar's first kural defines true shame as shrinking back from a wrongful deed, and Beck's resignation was exactly such a refusal to put his hand to a deed he found base.
1011._accuracy_note: A clear case of recoiling from a wrong act out of conscience, though the sources speak of conscience and protest rather than of shame as such.

1012.event_title: Darwin calls blushing the most human of all expressions
1012.event: In The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals, published by John Murray in 1872, Charles Darwin gave a whole chapter to self-attention, shame, shyness, modesty and blushing. He opened it with the sentence "Blushing is the most peculiar and the most human of all expressions," and argued that no animal could be shown to blush.
1012.explanation: A founder of modern biology concluded that the outward sign of shame is the one expression that sets humans apart from other animals.
1012.tie_back: The kural says food and clothing are common to all living beings and that shame is what distinguishes humans; Darwin reached a strikingly similar conclusion from the study of expression.
1012._accuracy_note: Darwin's claim that the sign of shame is uniquely human closely mirrors the kural, though he wrote as a naturalist about blushing, not about the moral virtue of shame.

1013.event_title: JAL's president takes responsibility after the Flight 123 crash
1013.event: On 12 August 1985 a Japan Air Lines Boeing 747 crashed into a mountain in Gunma Prefecture, the worst single-aircraft accident in history up to that time. JAL president Yasumoto Takagi apologised in person to the victims' relatives, publicly accepted responsibility for the accident and told Prime Minister Yasuhiro Nakasone that he would resign; a successor was named later that year.
1013.explanation: Time noted that Japanese leaders considered it ethically required to leave office when something went disastrously wrong on their watch, even without direct personal fault.
1013.tie_back: The kural makes shame the very seat of nobility, as the body is the seat of life, and Takagi's response showed a leader's standing resting on his readiness to feel and answer for a disgrace.
1013._accuracy_note: Shows dignity of office joined to a sense of shame and responsibility, but it illustrates the kural's link between nobility and shame indirectly rather than dramatising it.

1014.event_title: Turkmenistan's ruler raises a revolving gold statue of himself
1014.event: In 1998 President Saparmurat Niyazov, who styled himself Turkmenbashi, 'Father of all Turkmen', built the Arch of Neutrality in Ashgabat, crowned with a gold-coloured statue of himself that rotated so as to face the sun throughout the day. He also renamed the months of the year after himself and members of his family. After his death his successor restored the old month names and removed the statue from the city centre in 2010.
1014.explanation: The monument became a world-famous emblem of pomp without restraint, and it was quietly dismantled once its builder was gone.
1014.tie_back: The kural warns that without shame the proud, stately bearing of the great becomes a sickness to behold, and Niyazov's self-glorifying statue was such a display.
1014._accuracy_note: Fits the kural's picture of proud display lacking modesty; the sources describe the self-glorification without passing explicit moral judgment.

1015.event_title: Gandhi calls off his campaign after the violence at Chauri Chaura
1015.event: On 4 February 1922 a crowd of protesters in Chauri Chaura, in the United Provinces, set fire to a police station and 22 policemen died. Although Gandhi was far away and had not ordered it, he called the episode a sign that the country was not ready, suspended the mass civil disobedience he had planned to launch from Bardoli, and fasted as a penance; Britannica records that he described his own launch of the campaign as a "Himalayan blunder."
1015.explanation: Gandhi treated a wrong done by others in the name of his movement as his own fault, to the dismay of many colleagues who wanted the campaign to continue.
1015.tie_back: The kural praises those who feel ashamed of others' wrongs as of their own, and Gandhi's penance for the deed of a distant crowd is a near-literal example.
1015._accuracy_note: Gandhi took public responsibility and did penance for violence committed by others, almost exactly the kural's 'dwelling-place of shame'.

1016.event_title: Nelson Mandela rejects a conditional release from prison
1016.event: On 31 January 1985 State President P. W. Botha offered Nelson Mandela, in prison since the Rivonia Trial, his release on condition that he renounce violence as a means of political change. Mandela refused, and on 10 February 1985 his daughter Zindzi read his written reply to a rally at Jabulani Stadium in Soweto, where he said he could not accept freedom while his organisation remained banned and his people were not free.
1016.explanation: Mandela chose to remain in prison, where he stayed for five more years, rather than accept personal freedom on terms he considered dishonourable to his cause.
1016.tie_back: The kural says the truly great would not take even the wide world without the hedge of shame, and Mandela declined freedom itself rather than accept it on dishonouring terms.
1016._accuracy_note: Strong illustration of refusing a great gain at the cost of honour, though Mandela framed it in political rather than personal terms.

1017.event: After years of imprisonment and trial by the Roman Inquisition, the philosopher Giordano Bruno declared that he had nothing to retract. Pope Clement VIII ordered him sentenced as an impenitent heretic; the sentence was read to him on 8 February 1600, and he was executed in the Campo de' Fiori on 17 February 1600.
1017.explanation: Bruno is remembered as a person who gave up his life rather than disown the convictions he held, and a statue was raised to him at the place of his execution in 1889.
1017.tie_back: The kural says those who live by shame will give up life for its sake but never give it up to save life, and Bruno would not recant even to escape death.
1017._accuracy_note: A clear choice of death over self-abasement; the exact doctrines for which he was condemned are debated, but his refusal to recant is not.

1018.event_title: Joseph Welch asks Senator McCarthy whether he has any sense of decency
1018.event: During the televised Army-McCarthy hearings, Senator Joseph McCarthy publicly accused Fred Fisher, a young lawyer in the firm of Army counsel Joseph Welch, of past links to a group he called a Communist front. Welch rebuked him before the cameras, ending with the question "Have you no sense of decency?", and the hearing room broke into applause. In December 1954 the Senate voted to condemn McCarthy's conduct.
1018.explanation: The exchange is widely seen as the turning point at which public opinion turned against McCarthy.
1018.tie_back: The kural says that a man who feels no shame at what would shame others is abandoned by virtue itself, and McCarthy's standing collapsed soon after he was publicly shown to lack that shame.
1018._accuracy_note: Welch's question names the exact failing the kural describes, and McCarthy's swift fall fits the abandonment reading.

1019.event_title: Boris Onishchenko's rigged epee gets the Soviet pentathlon team thrown out
1019.event: During the fencing stage of the modern pentathlon at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, officials found that Soviet pentathlete Boris Onishchenko's epee had been modified with a hidden switch that could register a hit without any touch. He was disqualified from the Games and banned from the sport, and his disqualification also put the whole Soviet team out of the competition.
1019.explanation: A single act of dishonesty ruined a decorated athlete's career and cost his teammates, who had done nothing wrong, their place in the event.
1019.tie_back: The kural says a lapse in conduct burns the name of one's 'family', and Onishchenko's cheating brought down his team along with himself.
1019._accuracy_note: Fits the first line well (one lapse ruining the wider group); the second line's settled shamelessness is only implied.

1020.event_title: Puyi is installed as head of Japanese-controlled Manchukuo
1020.event: After the Japanese army occupied Manchuria in 1931, Japan created the state of Manchukuo in March 1932 and brought Puyi, the last Qing emperor, from Tianjin to serve as its chief executive; he was enthroned as emperor in 1934. Although Manchukuo was proclaimed independent, its government was controlled and supervised by the Japanese, and the League of Nations refused to recognise it.
1020.explanation: Manchukuo became the classic example of a puppet state, with a figurehead ruler moved by others.
1020.tie_back: The kural likens those without inner shame to a wooden puppet worked by strings to look alive, and Puyi in Manchukuo was a ruler in appearance only, moved by outside hands.
1020._accuracy_note: Matches the puppet image vividly, but the sources describe political control, not Puyi's lack of shame, so the moral half of the kural fits only partly.
